children: Chicago soybean and corn futures extended losses on Wednesday, as funds exited long positions and US farmers accelerated harvesting of large crops.
Wheat followed lower on technical and fund selling.
FUNDAMENTALS
* The most-traded soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
fell 0.1% to $12.47 a bushel by 0051 GMT, hovering near its lowest in eight weeks.
* CBOT corn
slid 0.11% to $4.61-1/2 a bushel, while wheat
fell 0.35% to $6.41 a bushel, hitting a more-than-two-month low.

* Forecasts for favourable harvest weather across the Midwest through at least the end of the week weighed on crop markets, as farmers brought in a record-large soybean crop and what is expected to be the second-largest US corn harvest on record.
* Harvest pressure outweighed support from renewed Chinese demand as the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) confirmed more purchases by the world's top soy importer.
* US farmers have harvested 64% of the soybean crop and 44% of the corn crop, according to the USDA's weekly crop progress report released on Monday. Both figures were below trade expectations.
* Winter wheat planting was 63% complete, also below analysts' expectations of 65%.
* ANEC on Tuesday estimated Brazil's soybean exports at 6.40 million metric tons in October, down from its previous weekly estimate of 6.55 million tons.
* Wheat traders assessed disruptions to Black Sea grain exports from Russia's war in Ukraine.

* President Donald Trump said on Monday the USDA would launch what he called a new "harvest fuel relief program" that will provide farmers with $8 billion in support to offset diesel costs during harvest season.
* Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn, soybeans and wheat, traders said on Tuesday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
